title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Cowork for GCC and GCC High
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, GCC licensing, access requirements and government feature differences are supported. The web-search API needs a caveat about conflicting government-cloud documentation, and two settings paths should name the final control.

claims.claim: The worldwide policy documentation says users reaching a monthly limit lose selected-service access for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Limit enforcement is asynchronous and users might start tasks after reaching their limit.
claims.quote: Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: The worldwide access page says a low credit limit does not remove Cowork access.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: The worldwide access page says removing access requires removing a user from every spending policy that includes Cowork.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0]; Governance controls
claims.claim: The worldwide access rules grant Cowork access through any in-scope policy selecting Cowork and deny it if no such policy exists.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them ... and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services. If no policy in scope selects Cowork, the user has no access.

claims.claim: The GCC article warns that the worldwide spending-policy access procedure is not government setup guidance.
claims.quote: These are government prerequisites. The worldwide spending-policy access procedure in Determine access controls for Cowork isn't government setup guidance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The GCC page gives no credit rate for Cowork tasks.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cowork" "GCC" "credit rate". Read cowork-government in full, including licensing and billing prerequisites; it names funding methods and usage billing but gives no per-task credit rate.

claims.claim: The Graph create-spending-policy reference requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy lists Office Apps Administrator as recommended, alongside Security Administrator and Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) ... Security Administrator ... Global Administrator

claims.where: Scope: Rollout; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft directs GCC administrators to Message Center for their tenant's availability information.
claims.quote: Check Microsoft 365 Message Center for availability information for your tenant.

claims.claim: The group-scoped spending-policy path is Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Policy scope > Identity > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... choose Identity as the scope. ... switch to Specific groups and select the directory group. ... The Model templates step appears only when you select Cowork in a spending policy.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings adds a service setting to a spending policy.
claims.quote: Create a new spendingPolicyServiceSetting object to add a service to an existing spending policy. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b/serviceSettings

claims.claim: The service-setting API is beta and requires serviceId and state in its request body.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... Required properties are serviceId and state.

claims.claim: The create-service-setting reference example uses another serviceId and does not give a Cowork value.
claims.quote: Searched: read spendingpolicyservicesetting-create in full for Cowork/serviceId. Its request and response examples use researcherCritiqueAndCouncil, with no Cowork value; this narrow statement is about that reference, not all Graph documentation.

claims.claim: The web-search policy route in the Apps admin center ends at Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The existing route reaches the correct page; the final policy name is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access, already cited.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply a desired-state baseline in applyOnce mode.
claims.quote: applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors

claims.claim: The preview TCM resource for web search is microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch with resourceVersion 1 and properties.value.
The web-search resource value "0" enables search in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The web-search resource value "1" disables search in both Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: 1 disables it in both.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: A target Copilot setting must not also be configured in a group-level policy when using TCM.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.

claims.claim: The signed-in user needs the AI Administrator role for Copilot-setting applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for this applyOnce operation.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: TCM is available only in the global service, so the web-search applyOnce call is unavailable to GCC High.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta. TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.
claims.fix: Replace 'Global service only, not GCC High' in controls[1].note with 'Government-cloud availability differs between Microsoft pages; see below.' Replace the categorical global-only and GCC High exclusion sentences with: 'The remediation/applyOnce support page says TCM is available only in the global service, but the create-configurationMonitor reference lists US Government L4 and L5 as supported. Confirm web-search applyOnce availability for GCC High before relying on this API.' Both https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta are already cited.

claims.claim: GCC uses the worldwide Microsoft Graph endpoint.
claims.quote: If you're working in a Microsoft 365 GCC environment, continue using the worldwide endpoints: https://portal.azure.com and https://graph.microsoft.com.

claims.claim: GCC High uses graph.microsoft.us.
claims.quote: If you're working in a Microsoft 365 GCC High environment, use https://portal.azure.us and https://graph.microsoft.us.

claims.claim: The browser article gives Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings > Allow browser access.
claims.quote: From the menu, select Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings. ... Under Allow browser access, select Allow Cowork to use the Microsoft Edge browser to perform tasks on behalf of users.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings > Allow browser access > Allow Cowork to use the Microsoft Edge browser to perform tasks on behalf of users', as given at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/cowork/cowork-local-browser#admin-control. Keep the existing warning about conflicting GCC guidance.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for the Cowork tenant browser-access switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cowork" "Allow browser access" "Graph"; "Cowork" "Local Browsing Allowed" API PowerShell; Graph Cowork browsing; PowerShell Cowork browser. Read browser/admin articles and TCM resources. Edge policy controls browser instances, not this tenant switch.

claims.claim: The browser article's admin-control section says browser use is disabled by default.
claims.quote: For worldwide and GCC tenants, admins enable Cowork browsing by performing the following steps. This feature is disabled by default.

claims.claim: The browser article's admin-control section explicitly applies its path to worldwide and GCC tenants.
claims.quote: For worldwide and GCC tenants, admins enable Cowork browsing by performing the following steps.

claims.claim: The same browser article separately names a default-off Local Browsing Allowed policy for GCC.
claims.quote: In GCC, local browsing is governed by the default-off Local Browsing Allowed policy. ... The web address and admin click path below describe the worldwide experience.

claims.claim: The spending-policy page says Auto-apply new services is selected by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services automatically adds newly supported Copilot services and agents to a policy.
claims.quote: When a spending policy has Auto-apply new services turned on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy as they become available.

claims.claim: The GCC page does not say whether Auto-apply new services adds Cowork to existing GCC policies.
claims.quote: Searched: read cowork-government in full for spending policy, automatic enablement and Auto-apply new services; compared the cited spending-policy page. The GCC page gives manual setup prerequisites and no statement about Auto-apply new services.

claims.claim: GCC High administrators access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at config.office365.us.
claims.quote: US Government Community (GCC) High customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office365.us
